age_model_features.notes: Feature counts refer to the measured biomarkers. Sex was included separately in all three models as a binary indicator for male sex. The NMR panel comprised 168 absolute Nightingale measurements, and proteins are listed by their Olink assay labels. The routine blood panel comprised 31 haematological and 28 serum biochemical measurements. NMR, nuclear magnetic resonance.

healthy_reference_conditions.notes: The table lists the conditions and corresponding definitions used to identify the healthy reference population. Participants were classified as healthy if they had no recorded history of any listed condition at baseline. This population was used for age-model development, calibration and estimation of the age- and sex-specific reference distributions for standardizing BAG and BAU. BAG, biological age gap; BAU, biological age uncertainty; ICD-10, International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision.

covariate_definitions.notes: UK Biobank entries cover outcome, molecular, physiological and BAU determinant analyses, with covariates included as specified for each analysis in the Methods. External-cohort entries describe mortality models. Unknown or missing responses were retained as categories where listed. Longitudinal UK Biobank analyses required reported education and employment, while retaining an unknown household-income category. Missing values for CHNS ethnicity, residence, employment, education, health insurance and smoking were replaced with the most frequent category. NHANES mortality analyses were unweighted. BAU, biological age uncertainty; CHARLS, China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study; CHNS, China Health and Nutrition Survey; GED, General Educational Development; MEC, mobile examination centre; NHANES, National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.

additional_covariates.notes: BAU determinant models assessed the variation in BAU explained by measured factors. Missing medication responses were retained as missing values in BAU determinant models and handled directly by LightGBM. BAU, biological age uncertainty; BMI, body mass index; HDL, high-density lipoprotein.

health_outcomes.notes: Disease outcomes were identified from UK Biobank-derived first-occurrence records. Follow-up began at baseline or repeat assessment and ended at the target event, loss to follow-up, death or 31 December 2022. Incident outcome analyses included participants free of the corresponding outcome at the start of follow-up. Death was included in loss of healthspan and treated as a censoring event in Cox models of multimorbidity and individual diseases. H7 denotes the seven major disease domains listed above. Each domain counted once, and two domains first recorded on the same date defined multimorbidity on that date. ICD-10, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision.

external_feature_harmonisation.notes: Separate age models were developed in UK Biobank using the 24, 16 and 18 blood measurements available in NHANES, CHARLS and CHNS, respectively, with sex included in each model. The UK Biobank preprocessing, fitted models, sex-specific calibration and healthy-reference standardization were applied to the corresponding external cohort. Participants had fewer than 20% of panel measurements missing; remaining missing values were imputed using medians from the corresponding UK Biobank model-fitting sample. BAG and BAU were derived relative to chronological age and expressed on the UK Biobank healthy-reference scale. Conversions use values in the source units. For NHANES creatinine, values in mg dl⁻¹ were first corrected using 1.013 × value + 0.147 for 1999–2000 and 0.978 × value − 0.016 for 2005–2006, then multiplied by 88.4 to obtain μmol l⁻¹. BAG, biological age gap; BAU, biological age uncertainty; CHARLS, China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study; CHNS, China Health and Nutrition Survey; NHANES, National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.

physiological_traits.notes: In the discovery sample, each trait was winsorized at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles, transformed as indicated in the table and standardized using the mean and s.d. among healthy participants. The same winsorization thresholds, transformations and standardization parameters were applied to the validation sample from held-out assessment centres. Each trait was analysed among participants with an available measurement. BMD, bone mineral density; FEV1, forced expiratory volume in 1 s.
